points.description: Defines ESN as a type of recurrent neural network, i.e. it has feedback/cyclic connections (and/or only the output-layer weights are trained).
points.partial_credit: Half if vague, e.g. says it is a type of neural network with memory or loops but not clearly recurrent/feedback.

points.description: Says how it differs from FF NNs: ESN has feedback (cyclic) connections while FF NNs do not (so ESN can handle/approximate dynamic systems, FF NNs cannot).
points.partial_credit: Half if the difference is vague, e.g. ESN handles time/sequences better, without mentioning feedback connections.

rubric.notes: Full marks: says an ESN is a recurrent network with feedback connections, and that unlike FF NNs (no feedback) it can handle dynamic systems. Give part marks for vague but related answers, e.g. mentions memory, time series or only training the output weights without the feedback idea. Give no marks for wrong or unrelated answers. Technical terms are not required and extra remarks do not cost marks.
